title: flat C-step reorder: G2(t) moved ahead of G1(t+1) in the steady loop
status: REJECTED at Gate 2 (performance regression on all 3 shapes; well outside the 3% adoption threshold)

shipped_untouched.note: no Gate 3 was triggered; variant lives only in perf_tuning/gqa_flat_g2first_variant.py

design.source: cv_overlap_resurvey_iter3.md §8-C3 (cheap independent probe arm; low-confidence -0..-8%, sign unpredictable on paper)
design.implementation: generated from the shipped flat kernel block by gen_variants_iter4.py; full audit diff perf_tuning/diff_iter4_g2first.txt (1 hunk, +2/-2 lines: the steady-loop body swap + comment). Slots/tokens/counts/ids untouched — pure intra-step issue-order change.
design.static_safety_check: l0*/v_l1 parity of G2(t) (t%2) and G1(t+1) ((t+1)%2) disjoint; q_l1/p_l1 local-flag protocol order-preserving; K/V MTE2 loads of G1(t+1) now queue behind G2(t)'s ws_p read (accepted cost, measured); no new dependency cycle: G2(t)<-AO(t-1)<-G2(t-1)<-...<-init. The shipped epilogue was ALREADY G2-first, so the steady loop became consistent with it.

gates.gate0_standalone_precision: PASS 10/10 (perf_tuning/run_iter4_variant.py --arm g2first): same case list as C1 (3 in-gate A/B shapes, mc2 edges, mixed mc, padcol S_kv=100, causal S_kv>S, boundary NaN/Inf sparse). ALL finite cases bit_identical=True vs shipped gqa(); boundary struct-equal (NaN pos / Inf pos+sign / finite bits). Zero [gqa][fallback] lines.
gates.gate1_full_suite_monkeypatch: NOT RUN — deferred behind Gate 2 per pre-registered plan (arm rejected at Gate 2). Harness retained: perf_tuning/gate1_suite_iter4.py g2first.
gates.gate2_performance: FAIL — same-session three-way interleaved A/B (3 samples/arm/shape, all rated 1650/1650 MHz). C3 vs BASE: R3 75.05 vs 60.55 = +24.0% SLOWER; R2 28.69 vs 26.17 = +9.6% SLOWER; R6 30.61 vs 27.62 = +10.8% SLOWER. Rejected. Arm spreads tiny (0.3-3.2%) => verdict unambiguous.

measurements.data_quality_note: r3_g2first_s2 PipeUtilization.csv contained one impossible row (block19 aic_time=1395us vs TaskDur 75.14us) — profiler artifact; the row's block was excluded from wait-id/hot-core aggregation (all other samples clean). TaskDur (adoption metric) taken from OpBasicInfo.csv, unaffected.

mechanism_findings.intended_effect_FAILED: V_id3 (SM waiting for ws_p release — the target) is UNCHANGED on R3 (20.43 -> 21.44us): moving G2(t) to the step head does NOT release SM(x+2) earlier in practice, because C step t itself cannot start until its predecessor drains, and the strict data-ready chain (SM(x)->G2(x)->AO(x)->beat order->SM(x+2)) re-serializes the ring at the same cadence.
mechanism_findings.measured_side_effects: C_id1 nearly vanished (33.73 -> 2.34us: the G1 release-wait finds its token already pending after G2(t)'s chain), BUT (a) C_id5 exploded 12.27 -> 54.25us: G2(t)'s head-of-step WS3_V2C wait (AO(t-1) release) is now EXPOSED instead of hidden behind the old G1 pacing stall; (b) V_id0 rose 8.67 -> 22.29us: ws_s(t+1) FIX write lands later by ~dur(G2(t)) exactly as the resurvey's cost-side warned — and since V is the pacer on R3 (hot_aiv 57.6 -> 71.9us, +25%), delaying its data gate delays the whole kernel.
mechanism_findings.conclusion: The shipped G1-first step order is pacer-feed-first: it prioritizes ws_s production for V and hides G2's AO-release wait under G1's stall. C3's paper 'sign unpredictable' resolved decisively negative. No variant of this reorder is worth pursuing without also addressing the strict data-ready chain.

rollback_reason: Gate 2 regression on all 3 shapes (+24.0%/+9.6%/+10.8% vs same-session BASE); variant not adopted, gqa.py untouched. Artifacts retained: gqa_flat_g2first_variant.py, diff_iter4_g2first.txt, msprof_op_iter4_*_g2first_s{1..3}.
next_hint_iter5: Do not retry C-step reordering in the flat domain. C2 (kv==2 flat dual-stream): keep shipped step order G1(u+1)->G2(u), ns=2 slots, single release token; gain must come from deleting the g2stack batch-boundary drain/refill only.
